newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Thierry Daman read Commission President Jacques Santer's telegram to Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following Jerusalem's Shuk Mahane Yehuda bomb attack on Wednesday. Santer expressed his condolences to the families of the victims on his own and the Commission's behalf.
Daman said the Commission had invited Morocco's authorities to an extraordinary joint EU/Morocco Fisheries Committee meeting on August 11-13 in Brussels.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/730: Company taxation: European Commission pursues infringement proceedings against France and Greece.
- IP/97/731: Single market: infringement proceedings for failure to notify national measures transposing Community legislation.
- IP/97/732: Commission supports urban renewal in Brighton, Coventry, Bristol and Merseyside.
- IP/97/733: Three French regions receive Community aid worth ECU 273.4 million for industrial restructuring.
- IP/97/734: Free movement of goods: infringement procedures against Greece, Italy, Germany, Belgium, Sweden, the United Kingdom and Portugal.
- IP/97/735: Wide-screen TV action plan bows out - results of final call for proposals and World Cup football in wide-screen.
- Eurostat news release No 54/97: "Dynamic" EU trade with rest-of-world.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Agriculture, forestry and fisheries: Survey of the pig livestock population in April 1997.
